title: Characterisation of a nursery site for reef manta rays Mobula alfredi at Maamunagau Lagoon, Maldives
content:
Abstract

Nursery areas are critical habitats for early life stages of many marine species, yet few have been identified for reef manta rays Mobula alfredi, despite their vulnerable conservation status. The Maldives Archipelago supports the world's largest known population of M. alfredi, but no nursery area has previously been characterised. We evaluated whether the Maamunagau Lagoon (MMGL), Raa Atoll meets three elasmobranch nursery criteria: (1) young-of-the-year (YoY; disc width ≤2000 mm) and juveniles are encountered more frequently than elsewhere, (2) they remain for extended periods and (3) the area is used repeatedly across years. From 2019 to 2022, photo-identification and stereo-video photogrammetry (SVP) quantified YoY and juvenile relative abundance, residency and site fidelity at MMGL and 10 other aggregation sites in Raa Atoll. Overall, 2786 sightings of 354 individual M. alfredi were documented, and 292 SVP size measurements were obtained from 105 individuals. Sightings per unit effort (SPUE, sightings per survey day) were significantly higher at Inner MMGL for juveniles (4.11 ± 0.11) and YoY (0.78 ± 0.05) than at all other sites (p < 0.001). Across the study period, YoY showed higher seasonal residency indices (SRImin$$ {SRI}_{min} $$) at Inner MMGL (11.9% ± 1.2%) than at Fringing MMGL (4.1 ± 0.6%) and all regional sites (7.9% ± 1.4%). Multi-year site fidelity was evident, with 88.1% of YoY resighted beyond their initial identification season, and some individuals recorded for four consecutive seasons. These findings make Inner MMGL the first documented nursery area for M. alfredi in the Maldives and therefore a priority site for conservation evaluation.
